html:
The Rembarrnga are an Aboriginal people of central Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory, in stone country and river valleys inland from the coast.

Their neighbours include the Dalabon, the Ngalakan and the Yolngu peoples to the north and east. Their language is not part of the large Pama-Nyungan family that covers most of Australia. Arnhem Land is famous for its rock art and bark painting, and Rembarrnga artists have taken part in that tradition.

Because Arnhem Land became an Aboriginal reserve in 1931, the Rembarrnga kept close ties to their country. Some live at small outstations such as Bulman and Weemol. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Rembarrnga are an Aboriginal people of central Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory, in stone country and river valleys inland from the coast.
